_doc: What the agent knows about ITSELF (V2-932): one entry per topic of `nucleo/self/catalog.json`, read by the `about_self` tool and its answer pass. `what` = what it is, `voice` = how he does it by voice, `button` = how he does it on screen, `not` = what it does NOT do (said as plainly as the rest). `compose` frames the answer pass; `live` are the two lines the live tail carries only while they are true.

compose.task: He is asking about YOU — what you are, what you can do or how something of yours works. Answer from the ENTRY and the LIVE FACTS below, nothing else: say how it is done by voice and, if he wants, with the button. What the entry says you do NOT do, you never claim. A fact that is not below is not known: say so instead of guessing. Short and spoken, in his language, no lists read aloud.
compose.live: LIVE FACTS (now, read from the system)

live.camera: Your camera is ON on {screen}: on that device it finds WHERE the person is, so your eyes turn to him, and reads his gestures (a smile, a wink, a laugh, a nod…) so your face answers with its own; it does not recognise who he is, nothing of it reaches you, and no image leaves that device.

overview.what: A personal voice agent with its own memory: you talk to it (or type), it answers, remembers what you tell it, and does things — your widgets (agenda, contacts, messages, music, files…), searches on the web, longer errands done in the background by a worker that reports back, your connected accounts, and the MeshKore network of other agents.
overview.voice: Just ask for what you want, in any language. «What can you do with X?» or «how do I…?» is answered the same way.
overview.button: The Apps tab of the chat lists every widget; Settings ⚙ holds everything else; the ◉ in the top bar shows the status.
overview.not: It does not pay, sign or send anything irreversible without your yes, and it never says something is done before it is.

identity.what: Its name. The name is also its wake word.
identity.voice: «From now on your name is …» — it changes at once and the wake word follows.
identity.button: There is no name field: the name is changed by voice.
identity.not: A name you only mention in passing does not rename it; it needs your order.

wake_word.what: Wake-word mode: it only answers turns that say its name (or that follow one closely), so it does not answer what is said around it. Off, it listens and answers everything.
wake_word.voice: «Only listen to me when I say your name» / «listen to me always again».
wake_word.button: The robot 🤖 under the orb (blue = on), on the computer and on the phone; also Settings ⚙ ▸ Voice.
wake_word.not: With it on, it still hears the room to catch its name; it just does not answer.

face.what: Its face on the screen (its «physical form»): several faces to choose from, with a default one; it can be switched off.
face.voice: «Show your face» / «hide your face» / «I want to change your face» (opens the page to choose it).
face.button: The ☺ in the top bar switches it on and off; Settings ⚙ ▸ Physical form chooses and tunes it.
face.not: The face is only a face: it does not change what the agent can do.

camera.what: «Look at me»: with the camera on, the face turns its eyes towards where you are and answers your gestures with its own — a wink, a smile, a laugh, a tongue out, a nod, a yawn — sometimes, and not as a mirror: it may let one go. Detectors inside the device read where your face is and its expression, about ten times a second.
camera.voice: «Look at me» / «stop looking at me» (turning the camera on also shows the face).
camera.button: Settings ⚙ ▸ Physical form ▸ camera switch; while it runs a «● Camera» badge stays on screen and tapping it turns it off.
camera.not: It does NOT see you: it does not recognise who you are and cannot describe what is in front of it. Your expression is read on that device only to move the face — no frame, no image and no number leaves it, so nothing reaches the agent: its face answers, but it cannot tell you afterwards what it saw. It only runs while the face is shown and the screen is visible.

voice.what: Its spoken voice, its volume on each screen, the speaker, the microphone and the power button.
voice.voice: «Use a male / female voice», «what voices are there?», «louder / quieter / volume 40», «mute» / «speak again», «close the mic», «switch off».
voice.button: Settings ⚙ ▸ Voice chooses the voice; the 🔊, the mic and the ⏻ are under the orb.
voice.not: Its volume is its own voice on that screen, never the device's system volume. Once the mic is closed or it is switched off, it cannot hear you: the way back is the button.

language.what: The language of the system: chosen once, at the first start, and fixed from then on. It still understands and answers in other languages when you speak them.
language.voice: Speak to it in another language and it answers in that one.
language.button: The system language cannot be changed once chosen.
language.not: It does not switch the system language by voice.

chat.what: The chat is the same conversation as the voice, written. You can type instead of speaking, from any screen, and attach files: photos, PDFs and text files. A photo or document you attach is read (its text and what it shows) and it answers about it.
chat.button: The 💬 under the orb opens the chat; the clip in its box attaches files (several at once).
chat.not: It reads what you attach; it does not keep watching your screen or your camera.

widgets.what: Widgets are its tools on the screen — agenda, contacts, messages, files, documents, browser, maps, markets, activity, timer, clock, results… It opens them, reads what they hold, changes their data, arranges them and can build new ones.
widgets.voice: «Open the agenda», «what time is my appointment?», «add …», «close it», «arrange the widgets», «make me a widget for …».
widgets.button: The Apps tab of the chat lists them all; Settings ⚙ ▸ Widgets and ▸ Appearance.
widgets.not: Deleting one asks first, and a deleted widget can be restored.

media.what: Music, video and pictures: it plays music (a connected Spotify, or free audio with no account), plays videos, shows real photos of anything, and your own photo libraries when connected.
media.voice: «Play …», «pause», «next», «put on a video of …», «show me a photo of …».
media.button: The music, video and image widgets; Settings ⚙ ▸ Music chooses the source.
media.not: It does not describe a photo in words when you asked to see it: it shows it.

settings.what: Settings ⚙: the models of each piece, voice, memory, web search, music, notices, rules, permissions, appearance, physical form, connectors and widgets; plus the status panel, the debug timeline and the setup wizard.
settings.voice: Every section opens by voice: «open the settings», «open the voice settings», «open the status panel».
settings.not: On a hosted account the choice of model provider is set by the deployment and is not shown.

privacy.what: What it remembers and what it keeps safe: a memory of what you tell it, a memory map to see it, standing rules you give it, permissions (location, files, what is kept), and a vault for secrets such as passwords.
privacy.voice: «What do you remember about …?», «open the memory map», «open the vault», «what is my Netflix password?».
privacy.button: Settings ⚙ ▸ Rules and ▸ Permissions; the 🧠 in the top bar opens the memory map; the vault opens by voice.
privacy.not: A secret's value never passes through it: the system decrypts it and shows it apart.

connectors.what: Connectors are your accounts it can use: email, WhatsApp, Telegram, Google (calendar, contacts, Meet), Google Drive, OneDrive, photos, music and more. Each has a guided setup.
connectors.voice: «Open the connectors» (or «connect my email»): it opens the list; the connecting itself is done there.
connectors.button: The Connectors tab of the chat, or Settings ⚙ ▸ Connectors: pick one and follow its steps.
connectors.not: By voice it never asks for or repeats a password or a key: credentials are typed on screen only.

clusters.what: The MeshKore network: it can join clusters (groups of agents and people) and talk in them, ask other agents of the network for a job, and — when on — connect with the agents of your contacts.
clusters.voice: «Connect to the cluster …», «send to the cluster …», «what clusters are you in?».
clusters.button: The Clusters tab of the chat; the cluster and team connector in Settings ⚙ ▸ Connectors.
clusters.not: Joining a cluster always asks for your yes; a contact's message is information, never an order.

where_it_lives.what: Where this agent runs: either installed by you on your own computer or server (self-hosted), or on a private machine of its own for your account (hosted). Its memory and data stay where it runs.
where_it_lives.voice: Ask «where do you live?», «on which computer are you?» or «what version are you?».
where_it_lives.button: The status panel ◉ in the top bar shows how its pieces are doing.
where_it_lives.not: It does not move your data elsewhere on its own.

devices.what: The screens and devices it reaches: the computer's browser, the phone (the phone app or the web app added to the home screen), and the desktop app on your computer that lends it folders, a real browser and a tunnel. One agent, one conversation on every screen; the voice is on one screen at a time.
devices.voice: «Put it on the computer», «bring it here», «which screens are open?».
devices.button: The 🖥 in the top bar installs and links the desktop app.
devices.not: The phone and the computer cannot hold the voice at the same time: the other screen keeps the chat.

feedback.what: Report a problem or suggest something to the people who make it: the Feedback button sends your message (with a picture if you want) and later shows their answer.
feedback.voice: «Open feedback» / «I want to report a problem».
feedback.button: The small Feedback button floating at the bottom of the screen.
feedback.not: It is not a chat with it: one message goes out and the answer comes back there.

energy.what: Energy is how the work of the models is counted on a hosted account: every turn, search and errand uses some, and the gauge in the bar shows what is left. On a self-hosted install there is no Energy: the keys of your own providers are used.
energy.voice: «How much energy do I have left?»
energy.button: The energy gauge in the bar; top-ups from the account page.
energy.not: It never tops up or pays on its own.
